title: Inverse Functions
page_title: Inverse Functions | Cambridge (CIE) AS Maths Revision Notes 2022

blocks.md:
- An **inverse** **function** is the **opposite** to the original function
- It is denoted by **f**<sup>**-1**</sup>**(x)**
- An inverse only exists for **one**-to-**one** functions

blocks.alt: Inverse Functions Notes Diagram 1, A Level & AS Level Pure Maths Revision Notes

blocks.text: How do I sketch inverse functions?

blocks.md: - The graphs of a function and its inverse are reflections in the line** y = x**

blocks.text: What are the domain and range of inverse functions?

blocks.alt: Inverse Functions Notes Diagram 3, A Level & AS Level Pure Maths Revision Notes

blocks.md:
- The range of a function will be the domain of its inverse function
- The domain of a function will be the range of its inverse function

blocks.text: How do I use algebra to find an inverse function?

blocks.md:
- Set **y = f(x)** and make **x** the subject
- Then rewrite in function notation
- Domain is needed to fully define a function
- The range of **f** is the domain of **f**<sup>**-1**</sup> (and vice versa)

blocks.alt: Inverse Functions Notes Diagram 4, A Level & AS Level Pure Maths Revision Notes

blocks.text: How are inverse functions and composite functions related?

blocks.md:
- A function (**f**) followed by its inverse (**f**<sup>**-1**</sup>) will return the input (**x**)
- **ff**<sup>**-1**</sup>**(x) = f**<sup>**-1**</sup>**f(x) = x **(for all values of x)
